findings.title: Attack 6: a control rendered disabled before hydration (and with JavaScript off) looks exactly like the enabled control
findings.location: site/src/components/board/ToolFrame.svelte:269-282 (.control sets color, background and border; .control:disabled changes only cursor); same pattern in T10GeometryStudio.svelte:1398-1415, T11FoldingBench.svelte:624-643 (.tab), Board.svelte:258-278 (.hit), History.svelte:87, Predict.svelte:167, T01GameBoard.svelte:770 and every other component's :disabled rule
findings.claim: Every :disabled and [aria-disabled='true'] rule of the site changes only the cursor, and .control sets its own colour, background and border, overriding the browser's greying. So the disabled controls of the server markup, and the frozen boards after hydration, look the same as usable ones.
findings.expected: SPEC 7.4: 'Controls are rendered with the disabled attribute, which the island removes when it hydrates, so a control never looks usable before it is.' A disabled control differs visibly from its enabled state.
findings.observed: All 2021 buttons that hydration enables, on 22 routes, have the same computed colour, background, border colour, opacity, filter, text decoration and weight before and after hydration (as do 160 of 472 inputs; only selects and checkboxes grey). Example on /tools/geometry/: 'Root polytope', 'Coxeter plane', 'Copy link' and 'Download data' all read color rgb(26,26,26), background rgb(255,255,255), border rgb(26,26,26) solid, opacity 1, and give byte-identical element screenshots with JS off (disabled) and hydrated (enabled). The same holds on tools/fold (tab, reset, copyLink), M7 b1, M6 b8 and tools/board.
findings.reproduction: From b9b8504 plus the reproducer files: npm ci; npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> npx playwright test -c redteam/redteam-RT-06-playwright.config.ts site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-06-disabled-look.spec.ts (5 failed, each listing controls with identical style and screenshots)
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 7.4 'Without JavaScript' ('so a control never looks usable before it is'); 4.0 'Controls are present but disabled until the island has hydrated'; CONTRACTS 5.1 ToolFrame 'the control row rendered disabled until hydration'
findings.proposedFix: Give :disabled and [aria-disabled='true'] one shared visible treatment in the control styles (for example reduced opacity or a dashed border, plus cursor), so it also covers frozen boards. Adopt the reproducer as a regression test.

findings.title: Attacks 1 and 12, sibling of P3-RT-06-03: nojs.spec.ts accepts T10's ring board, or its hidden empty canvas box, as the default figure, so a blank T10 snapshot passes the run without JavaScript
findings.location: site/tests/e2e/nojs.spec.ts:60-124 (toolReport and figureProblems); T10GeometryStudio.svelte:969-982 (snapshot beside the hidden .drawing[role=img] canvas box and the ring Board)
findings.claim: The strengthened figure predicate never reads T10's figure, the SVG snapshot (data-out="snapshot"). It is satisfied first by the ring-setting Board (data-board-group with data-node buttons). Without that, it is satisfied by <div class="drawing" role="img" aria-label hidden><canvas>, because the predicate reads no visibility. Blank snapshots therefore pass nojs.spec.ts. The comparison sweep (snapshot text and pointsDrawn) and M7.spec.ts (svg with a title, counts only for b8) also pass them.
findings.expected: SPEC 7.4: the no-JavaScript run checks 'that the text, every default figure and every table are present', and canvas tools 'ship an SVG snapshot of their default view'. After every point and segment of the snapshot is removed, the predicate rejects the root.
findings.observed: With every circle and path removed from all T10 snapshots (svg, title and desc kept), toolReport accepts all 13 M7 roots and the tool route as "board". With the ring board removed as well, it accepts all 13 as "drawing" through the hidden canvas box.
findings.reproduction: From b9b8504 plus the reproducer files: npm ci; npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> npx playwright test -c redteam/redteam-RT-06-playwright.config.ts site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-06-nojs-t10-figure.spec.ts (3 failed)
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 7.4 'Without JavaScript'; 4 T10 'Without JavaScript the default projection is shown as an SVG image produced at build time'; RED-TEAM-COMMON 2 ('a test that would pass against an empty function')
findings.proposedFix: In toolReport, ignore figures that are hidden (checkVisibility) or that are input controls of a tool with a snapshot. For canvas tools, require the visible data-out="snapshot" svg to hold at least one point. Optionally compare snapshot circle counts with vertexCount in the sweep.

findings.claim: The data-measured rule leaves drawMs empty in the server markup, as decided. The words around it ('in', 'ms') are outside the measured element, so every T10 instance shows a sentence about a drawing time that does not exist before hydration or without JavaScript.

RT-FIX-P3-nojs-phase4 says the measured element is empty in the server markup, so its sentence should not show an empty measurement.

findings.reproduction: From b9b8504 plus the reproducer files: npm ci; npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> npx playwright test -c redteam/redteam-RT-06-playwright.config.ts site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-06-t10-drawms-text.spec.ts (2 failed)
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 4.0 'Works before and without JavaScript'; 8.1 P1; DECISIONS.md RT-FIX-P3-nojs-phase4 'data-measured marks an output that measures the reader's machine'
findings.proposedFix: Render the clause 'in N ms' only when drawMs is known, for example by keeping the words inside the data-measured element. Its presence-only comparison then still holds.
